clue.text: Gather that the bell has gone?

definitions.meaning: to gather people or animals together is to collect them in one place
in boxing the bell ends a round, so the round is finished

explanation.definitionFit: Collecting scattered cattle or suspects is a roundup, and a boxing round being over is the second, punning reading.

clue.text: Craft without a prow

indicators.note: a prow is the front of a boat, so the front letter of the word Craft is removed

explanation.surface: A boat built with no pointed bow at its front.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the C from the front of CRAFT leaves the answer, and the whole clue also describes a flat floating platform, which has no shaped bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple flat floating platform of logs or planks is a vessel with no shaped bow at its front.

clue.text: Yet such a description may be fair

definitions.text: Yet such a description may be fair

parts.words: Yet such a description may be fair
parts.note: fair can mean good-looking, so the opposite description seems a contradiction; but fair also means pale-haired or just, and a plain-looking person can be that

explanation.definitionFit: The word means unattractive, the opposite of fair in its sense of beautiful, though someone fair-haired could still be plain.

clue.text: Do without and give to others

definitions.meaning: to manage without something, as in getting along with no need of it
to hand out or distribute, as a pharmacist does medicines

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to do away with (as in 'with') and to distribute or hand out to people.

clue.text: Demonstration of spiritual strength

definitions.meaning: a showing that something is true, evidence
the alcoholic strength of spirits, measured on a scale, as in 100 degrees

explanation.definitionFit: Evidence establishing a fact is one sense; the strength rating of distilled spirits is the other.

clue.text: The cad is about to break off the engagement

indicators.note: about can mean around or out of order, signalling that these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rotter is on the point of ending his betrothal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface engagement is a betrothal, but the answer means to disengage, as troops withdraw from a battle. 'is' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate or withdraw from contact or a fight is to disengage, which is what pulling away from a battle means.

clue.text: Expect disturbance in bar

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters of Expect are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates trouble breaking out in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the preposition meaning 'apart from'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are prepositions meaning apart from or leaving out, as in 'all bar one'.

clue.text: It indicates I will be missing from "Who's Who"

definitions.text: It indicates I will be missing from "Who's Who"

parts.words: It indicates I will be missing from "Who's Who"
parts.note: in the contraction who's, a punctuation mark stands where the letter I of 'who is' has been dropped

explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark shows where letters are left out in a contraction, such as the dropped I of 'who is'.

clue.text: Thumbs up for a seeker of cheap travel

definitions.text: Thumbs up for a seeker of cheap travel

parts.words: Thumbs up for a seeker of cheap travel
parts.note: not approval but a roadside traveller holding up a thumb to ask motorists for a free lift

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who travels by begging free lifts from passing drivers is the cheap traveller pictured.

clue.text: The point of punctuation

parts.note: the purpose of punctuation seems meant, but it is literally a dot, the punctuation mark ending a sentence

explanation.definitionFit: The dot ending a sentence is a point, the British name for what Americans call a period.

clue.text: Current charge for what solicitors do

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a cost is a price or fee charged

explanation.surface: A lawyer's fee arrangement described as current billing.
explanation.walkthrough: Solicitors look like British lawyers, but here they are people soliciting, such as street prostitutes, who approach strangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaching and addressing strangers boldly, as people touting for business do, is to waylay them.

clue.text: Current binder for correspondence

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a cord is a string used to tie or bind things

explanation.surface: Ongoing ties used to bundle up letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' suggests letters but means agreement or matching.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence can mean agreement or harmony between things, which the answer also means.

clue.text: Ideal sales talk of appeal to music lovers

parts.note: ideal means flawless, without fault
a pitch is a salesman's persuasive patter

explanation.surface: A flawless sales patter aimed at music fans.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the gift of naming any note heard is something music lovers prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The ability to identify or sing any note without reference is a musical gift admired by music enthusiasts.

clue.text: Hold up close to Cork

definitions.meaning: a hold-up is a delay or congestion in traffic
the narrow top of a wine bottle sits right next to its stopper

explanation.definitionFit: A traffic jam point causing delay is one sense; the narrow part of a bottle beside the stopper is the literal one.

clue.text: A pop star, perhaps, pulsating with vitality

definitions.meaning: an idol whom fans swoon over, a pop singer being an example
the beat of a living heart is a pulse

explanation.definitionFit: A swoon-inducing idol is one sense, and the literal beat of a heart is the other.

clue.text: Free fall may be enjoyed by sportsmen

parts.note: open means free, unrestricted
fall is the American word for autumn, a season

explanation.surface: Sporting types enjoying a free fall, like skydivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free fall' suggests skydiving; split it, and 'sportsmen' are hunters, who enjoy the period when shooting game is permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: The time of year when hunting a species is legal is enjoyed by shooting and fishing sportsmen.

clue.text: A panel on an aircraft, perhaps

parts.note: a board is a flat panel of wood

explanation.surface: A section of fuselage fitted to a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a plane, ship or train as a passenger is to be on board it.

clue.text: Charming feature of Japanese dress

parts.note: an attractive part of a kimono outfit, namely the broad sash tied round the waist; the word also means a sorcerer's charm, as obeah

explanation.definitionFit: The wide sash tied around a kimono is a key element of traditional Japanese costume.

clue.text: Aunt Enid flounders in swamp

indicators.note: to flounder is to struggle clumsily, so the letters of Aunt Enid tumble about

explanation.surface: A relative struggles helplessly in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swamp' looks like a noun, a bog, but is a verb meaning to flood.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to flood or overwhelm, the same as the verb meaning to deluge.

clue.text: The pitch of the road

parts.note: not the slope of a road but the black sticky substance spread on road surfaces

explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is the black viscous material used to surface roads, a synonym of this word.

clue.text: One may put one's foot in it; how does one wriggle out?

definitions.text: One may put one's foot in it; how does one wriggle out?

parts.words: One may put one's foot in it; how does one wriggle out?
parts.note: putting one's foot in it is a blunder, but here it is literal: a carved clog that one steps into and slips out of

explanation.definitionFit: A clog carved from a single block of timber, like a sabot, is footwear one literally steps into.

clue.text: Pop's executors?

parts.note: not those handling a dead father's will, but bands who perform popular music

explanation.definitionFit: Bands perform, or execute, pop music, so collections of musicians are the 'executors'.

clue.text: Bold break-in using a jemmy?

parts.note: to break in is to enter a building
a jemmy is a burglar's crowbar used for prising things open

explanation.surface: A daring burglary carried out with a crowbar.
explanation.walkthrough: A jemmy is the British word for a burglar's short crowbar (a jimmy in America).
explanation.definitionFit: Showing initiative and boldness in undertaking new ventures is what this adjective means.

clue.text: It can't run, so takes cover

parts.note: a lid is the cover of a pot or box

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot flee, so hides under shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like fleeing but means flowing like a liquid; 'takes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance in this state holds its shape and does not flow, unlike a liquid that runs.

clue.text: Crazy, maybe, but often with motive

definitions.meaning: a slang word for mad, from Spanish
the short form of a railway engine, which in full is followed by the word motive

explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for mad, and the shortened form of the word for a railway engine, which in full adds 'motive'.

clue.text: Impressive plea for original expression

parts.note: impressive here relates to printing impressions: a proofreader's instruction asking that the original wording be kept

explanation.definitionFit: This Latin proofreading mark means 'let it stand', telling the printer to keep the original text.

clue.text: Terrible, but not initially loud, stream of abuse

indicators.note: the loud letter is dropped from the start of the word meaning terrible

parts.note: terrible and fearful both mean dreadful
f (forte) is the musical abbreviation for loud

explanation.surface: An awful tirade, though not delivered loudly at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A long scolding or torrent of angry words is what one gets when told off at length.

clue.text: Get away with a clip round the ear

indicators.note: round tells us the blow goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a clip round the ear is a cuff, a clout
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to go, with a smack on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'clip round the ear' is British for a light smack on the head, but 'round' is the container signal. 'with', 'a' and 'the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave in a hurry, or be told to go away, is an informal sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Finally dispose of most of the relatives? Rot!

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
bosh and rot both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at the idea of getting rid of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is used as in 'put the kibosh on', to finish something off.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a stop to something decisively is to scupper or end it, the sense of this slang verb.

clue.text: Poor side away from home fails to survive

indicators.note: poor suggests something badly made, signalling that the letters of side are rearranged

parts.note: out means not at home

explanation.surface: A weak team playing an away fixture fails to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' is a sports team in the surface; in the wordplay its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: When a species or tradition fails to survive it becomes extinct, as the phrasal verb means.
